records.question: What are the two main processes of sexual reproduction in tropical corals?
ground_truth_chunks: Sexual reproduction in tropical corals occurs through one of two main processes:
Broadcast spawning involves the release of large numbers of gametes (eggs and sperm) into the water column over a short period of time (see Box 1 for a description of the spawning process).
Brooding involves internal fertilisation and the release of fully developed planulae.

records.question: When does coral spawning take place on the Great Barrier Reef and other reefs in the Indo-Pacific?
records.ground_truth_answer: Once a year during the week following the full moon in late spring or early summer.
ground_truth_chunks: On the Great Barrier Reef and other reefs in the Indo-Pacific, coral spawning takes place once a year during the week following the full moon in late spring or early summer (Harrison et al. 1984).

All colonies of each species usually spawn on a particular night during this week, and the timing is predictable from year to year (e.g. *Acropora* spp usually spawn on the 4<sup>th</sup> night after the full moon, *Platygyra* spp usually spawn on the 5<sup>th</sup> night etc.).

records.question: On which dates were coral spawning observations made?
records.ground_truth_answer: On five nights from November 9 to 13, 1995.
ground_truth_chunks: Coral spawning observations were made on five nights from November 9 to 13, 1995, which spanned three to seven days after the full moon.

records.question: At what time did most Porites cylindrica corals spawn at the Faga'alu lagoon site?
ground_truth_chunks: Fifteen to twenty *P. cylindrica* colonies were observed releasing milky clouds of sperm in the shallow lagoon site at Faga'alu on the third night after the full moon.
At 2035 hrs (2:15 after sunset), most of the corals spawned simultaneously with a few spawning over the next 20 minutes.

records.question: At what time after sunset and on which night after the full moon was *Acropora formosa* observed spawning at Faga'alu?
records.ground_truth_answer: It was observed spawning from 2020-2120 hrs (2 –3 hours after sunset) on the fourth night after the full moon.
ground_truth_chunks: This species is often called staghorn coral, and forms large thickets (each 4-5m in diameter) in the shallow lagoon at Faga'alu.
*Acropora formosa* was observed spawning from 2020-2120 hrs (2 –3 hours after sunset) on the fourth night after the full moon.

records.section_heading: Montipora turgescens and M. grisea (Family Acroporidae)
records.question: What were the observed spawning times (clock time and minutes after sunset) for Montipora turgescens and M. grisea?
records.ground_truth_answer: Montipora turgescens spawned between 1945 and 2030 (1:25 to 2:10 after sunset); M. grisea spawned at 2045 (2:25 after sunset).
ground_truth_chunks: *Montipora turgescens* spawned between 1945 and 2030 (1:25 to 2:10 after sunset).
*M. grisea* spawned at 2045 (2:25 after sunset).

records.question: How large were the egg-sperm bundles released by Merulina ampliata?
ground_truth_chunks: This species is hermaphroditic and released large (approx. 2mm diameter) pink egg-sperm bundles which could be seen setting for 10 minutes prior to their release.

records.question: When did the majority of male Stichopus chloronotus spawn relative to sunset?
records.ground_truth_answer: Between 1830 and 1900, which is 10 to 40 minutes after sunset.
ground_truth_chunks: The majority of males spawned between 1830 and 1900 (10 to 40 minutes after sunset) while the females did not begin spawning until 1850 (50 minutes after sunset).
Males intermittently released small continuous streams of sperm from the goniopore (reproductive opening), each lasting approximately 5 minutes.

records.section_heading: Patterns of spawning of corals and other invertebrates in American Samoa
records.question: On which night after the full moon did Porites cylindrica spawn at Faga'alu in 1995?
records.ground_truth_answer: On the 3rd night after the full moon, about 2 hours after sunset.
ground_truth_chunks: Itano and Buckley observed several colonies of *Porites cylindrica* spawning 2 hours after sunset on the 3<sup>rd</sup> night after the full moon at Nu'uuli in 1988. records.section_heading: The importance of coral spawning in marine resource management
records.question: How does increased sedimentation affect the development and settlement of coral larvae after spawning?
records.ground_truth_answer: Increased sedimentation strongly impairs larval development and settlement: 77% fewer embryos develop normally in water from sediment-stressed reefs; a sediment layer can prevent planulae settlement or force settlement into unsuitable microhabitats; and increased sedimentation can reduce survival of newly settled corals in the first months after settlement due to smothering and abrasion.
ground_truth_chunks: The development of coral embryos through to competent planulae appears to be affected by water quality, with 77% fewer embryos developing normally in water from sediment stressed reefs (Richmond 1994).
A layer of sediment on the reef surface can also prevent settlement of coral planulae, or restrict settlement of planulae to unsuitable microhabitats (Babcock and Davies 1991, Te 1992).
Increased sedimentation may also reduce the survival rate of newly settled corals in the first few months after settlement (Sato 1985) due to smothering and abrasion.
